purpose: Glipizide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is used along with a healthy diet and exercise to keep your blood sugar from getting too high. It is not used for type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.
how_it_works: Your pancreas makes a hormone called insulin, which helps move sugar out of your blood and into your body's cells for energy. Glipizide works by telling your pancreas to release more insulin, especially after meals. This helps bring your blood sugar down to a healthier level.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can make you feel shaky, sweaty, dizzy, confused, or very hungry — so always carry a fast-acting sugar like glucose tablets or juice. You may also experience nausea, upset stomach, or skin reactions like rash or itching. Some people notice mild weight gain.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to sulfa drugs, as you may also be allergic to glipizide. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can cause a sudden dangerous drop in blood sugar. Use caution in hot weather or during illness, as these can affect your blood sugar. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems may require a dose adjustment.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken once daily, about 30 minutes before breakfast. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose depending on how your blood sugar responds, up to a maximum of 40 mg per day. The extended-release tablet (Glucotrol XL) is taken once daily with breakfast. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
